references.body:
# Queue consumer limits

## Notes
- The consumer ack timeout defaults to 30 seconds per message.
- Prefetch defaults to 50 messages per channel.

# Broker connection limits

## Notes
- The broker closes a connection that sends no heartbeat for 60 seconds.
- A closed connection requeues every unacked message on it.

messages.content: Some orders are charged twice. The payment handler runs twice for the same message. Find out why.

I read the queue consumer limits and broker connection limits references. The broker reference rules out a dropped connection: heartbeats are steady. The consumer reference gives a 30 second ack timeout, and the slow payment handler takes about 45 seconds, so the broker redelivers the message while the first delivery is still running. Root cause: ack timeout shorter than the handler time.
Confirmed on the bench: raising the ack timeout to 90 seconds stops the double charge.

findings.summary: The consumer ack timeout (30s) is shorter than the payment handler time (~45s); the broker redelivers the message mid-handler and the order is charged twice.
